newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan bank shares falling, prospects gloomy.
newsitem.headline: Japan bank shares falling, prospects gloomy.

text.p: Many Japanese bank shares continued falling on Friday with the Nikkei banking sector index briefly hitting a low for the year.

Brokers and financial analysts said the selling pressure would remain on the banking sector at least until the end of the current fiscal year due to the problem loan mess and corporate investors' selling to unwind cross-shareholdings.
At 0417 GMT, the Nikkei banking sector index was at 3,394.02, down from the year's lowest closing of 3,395.64 on Thursday. The index fell to the year's trading low of 3,580.64 earlier.
By 0500 GMT, the price of Tokyo Sowa Bank Ltd shares had dropped 70 yen to 450 yen while shares in Hanshin Bank Ltd were down 26 yen at 296 yen.
Sakura Bank Ltd fell 14 yen to 933 yen, Hokkaido Takushoku Bank Ltd were down 1 yen at 221 yen and Nippon Credit Bank Ltd was off three yen at 300.
All of which were among the most-heavily traded issues.

Hideichiro Nishimura, an analyst at Yamaichi Research Institute of Securities and Economics Inc, said he expects the banking sector to remain under pressure until corporate investors complete the unwinding of their cross-shareholdings with banks and until banks complete their capital raising requirements by issuing new shares.

A second-tier brokerage analyst said that he expects the selling of bank shares to continue until the end of the current business year as corporate investors are likely to sell bank shares to rebuild their asset quality.
